title: Owner reporting and monthly statements (boundaries)
audience: Home-based property managers who report to owners on the condition, work and costs of their properties
learningOutcomes: Build a monthly owner report from the asset register, service records and approved work.
Separate reported facts from estimates, opinions and unresolved items.
State the boundaries of the report, including any financial handling that is not covered by this course.
referencesAtStart: Official sources: NSW Government, Real estate agent licence (published 27 June 2025; last modified 20 October 2026); NSW Government, Rental bonds for tenants (published 6 September 2023; last modified 16 September 2026); NSW Government, Real estate trust accounts and audit requirements (published 4 June 2025; last modified 2 June 2026); Queensland Government, Apply for a resident letting agent licence (last updated 26 October 2026). The reporting format in this lesson is working practice, not a regulatory rule.

instruction.heading: A report is built from records
instruction.body: A monthly owner report is built from the records already kept: the asset register, the service records, the approved work and the open items. Each figure or statement in the report should trace back to a dated record that the owner can ask to see. Do not write a report from memory, because memory can drop a visit, mix two properties or repeat an old finding as if it were new. Start by pulling the records for the period, then write each line from its record and note the record reference. A report that a reader can trace is worth more than a longer one that cannot be checked. Keep a fixed layout, with the same sections in the same order every month, so that owners can compare one month with the next.

instruction.heading: Separating what is known from what is proposed
instruction.body: Separate what is known from what is estimated, recommended or still open. A completed item is one that a dated record shows as done. A proposed repair is a recommendation, not a completed item, and it goes in its own section with the quote or estimate that supports it. An unresolved defect is an open item, not a closed one. Where the report includes an opinion, such as a view that a fixture will need replacing soon, label it as an opinion, say who gave it and on what evidence. Show a repair as in progress only if a record shows that work has started. Each section should make clear whether the reader is reading a record, an estimate or a view.

instruction.heading: Money in the report and its boundaries
instruction.body: Where the report includes money, state the source of each amount and whether it is an invoice, an estimate or a payment. An invoice is a request for payment, an estimate is a projection that may change, and a payment is money received or made. Do not mix them in one line. Handling of rent, deposits, bonds or trust money is not covered in this course. In New South Wales, a licensee keeps client money in a trust account, and that money may be used only for the client it belongs to. The licensee's trust records also go to an audit each year. The NSW licensing page lists collecting bonds and rents tied to a lease among the licensed functions for certain licence classes, and the NSW bond page caps a bond at four weeks' rent. In Queensland, a resident letting agent licence allows the holder to collect rents in the complex and to operate a trust account. Do not carry out or report financial handling until the rules for the state are confirmed, the licence position is confirmed, and the owner has agreed the process in writing.

instruction.heading: What the report is not
instruction.body: The report is a record of the property and the work, prepared for the owner. It is not an audit of the accounts, not a financial statement, and not a certificate of safety or compliance. A report that says a system is compliant must show the certificate or record that supports it, issued by the person or body authorised to issue it. A report that says nothing about an item should not be read as a statement that the item is fine. State each boundary in the report, so that the owner knows what the report can and cannot support.

procedure: Pull the records for the period: asset register changes, service records, approved work and open items.
Write each report line from a dated record, and note the record reference beside it.
Separate completed work, estimates, recommendations, opinions and open items into distinct sections.
State the source of each amount, and whether it is an invoice, an estimate or a payment.
Note any financial handling outside this course as not covered, and refer it to the owner for a written process.
State the boundaries of the report, including that it is not a certificate or an audit.
Send the report to the owner, and keep a copy on file with the records it was built from.

workedExamples.situation: An owner asks for the monthly report to show that a pump is repaired and running well.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should the report say about the pump?
workedExamples.reasoning: State the repair as completed only if the service record shows it, and give the date and the record reference. Do not state it as running well unless a record shows that it has been run and checked. If the owner asks for a view on how long it will last, label it as an opinion, say who gave it and on what basis.

workedExamples.situation: An owner asks for the report to show the rent received for the month, and the owner wants the figure to appear next to the repair costs.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Can the report show the rent figure, and what must be settled first?
workedExamples.reasoning: Not in this course. Rent handling is outside the course, and the licence and trust-account rules for the state must be confirmed first. In New South Wales, client funds must be held in trust and used only for the client, so the figure cannot be shown as if it were the property manager's income. Tell the owner that the rent figure is not covered here, and agree in writing how any financial figure will be provided, from whose records and under which rules. Keep the repair costs on their own invoice lines until that process is agreed.

equipmentAndPpe: Report template with fixed sections in a fixed order
Invoice, estimate and payment records, kept separately
Owner's written agreement to the reporting format

commonErrors.prevention: Build each line from a dated record, and note the record reference beside it.

commonErrors.error: Reporting a proposed repair as completed.
commonErrors.prevention: Separate completed work from recommendations, estimates and open items.

commonErrors.error: Stating an amount without its source.
commonErrors.prevention: State whether each amount is an invoice, an estimate or a payment, with its record.

commonErrors.error: Presenting an opinion as a finding.
commonErrors.prevention: Label each opinion, name its source and state the evidence it rests on.

commonErrors.error: Implying a certificate or a compliance result the record does not show.
commonErrors.prevention: State only what the record shows, and refer any compliance statement to the certificate that supports it.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Handling rent, deposits, bonds or trust money: In New South Wales the real estate agent licence page lists collecting bonds, deposits and rents in connection with a lease among the licensed functions for certain classes. NSW caps a bond at four weeks' rent. In NSW, licensees keep client money in a trust account, and that money is used only for the client it belongs to. Do not handle or report such money until the state rules and the licence position are confirmed.
Completing this lesson does not give a real estate, accounting or trust-handling licence or authority, and it does not authorise any handling of client money.
A report is not a certificate of compliance or safety. Any statement that an item complies must be supported by the certificate or record issued by the authorised person or body.

qualityStandard: Every report line traces to a dated record, with its reference.
Completed work, estimates, recommendations, opinions and open items are separated and labelled.
Each amount states its source and whether it is an invoice, an estimate or a payment.
Financial handling outside this course is noted as not covered, and the report states its boundaries.
documentationEvidence: Monthly owner report with a record reference for each line
Copy of the report filed with the records it was built from
Written owner agreement to the reporting format and to any financial figures included
Record of any opinion, with its source
summary: Build each report line from a dated record, and note the reference.
Keep completed work, estimates, recommendations, opinions and open items apart.
State the source of each amount, and do not mix invoices, estimates and payments.
Leave rent and trust handling outside the report until the state rules and the licence position are confirmed and the owner has agreed the process.

knowledgeChecks.question: A pump repair was recommended but not yet carried out. How should the report show it?
options: As completed, since it was recommended and the work is nearly done in the house today
Left out of the report, since the work has not started yet at the property today
As a recommendation, separate from completed work and with its supporting estimate
As a completed item with a note that it may be done later on by the trade team today

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should each report line cite a dated record?
options: Because owners only read the dates
It is not required if the report is short
So that each statement can be checked

knowledgeChecks.question: An owner asks for rent received to appear in the monthly report. What is the correct response in this course?
options: Show it as income with no source for the figure or the period, since the owner has asked for it to be shown this month in the report
Show it, since the owner asked for it and the owner pays for the report every month for the whole property portfolio
Note that rent handling is not covered here, and agree the process in writing once the state rules and licence position are confirmed
Show it as an estimate so nobody can check it, which keeps the report neat and tidy for the owner and the tenant alike
